description: Plain-JS gotchas in the worker (SSR pages, options objects, prototypes)

entries.bad_pattern: Destructuring an options object with a default whose key collides with an Object.prototype method, e.g. const { valueOf = (r) => r.key } = opts
entries.good_pattern: Name option keys so they never collide with Object.prototype members (valueOf, toString, hasOwnProperty, constructor, isPrototypeOf, ...). e.g. rename valueOf -> keyOf
entries.description: A destructuring default only applies when the read property is `undefined`. Properties named like Object.prototype methods are NEVER undefined — `({}).valueOf` resolves to the inherited native function via the prototype chain — so the default is skipped and the binding becomes the native method. Calling it (e.g. valueOf(row)) then throws 'Cannot convert undefined or null to object' (native valueOf called with this=undefined). This passed `node --check` (it's a runtime TypeError, not a syntax error) and 500'd every /reviews request until the option was renamed valueOf -> keyOf. Lesson: never name an options key after an Object.prototype member; and DB-less render code should get a quick mock-render smoke test since unit tests on pure builders won't catch it.
